title: 3.7.16 Plain English to Pseudocode: Spread vs. Rest, Side by Side
description: Turn five plain-English steps into pseudocode for the body of total(...numbers): the same gathering loop whether the caller spreads an array or lists the numbers.

planChart.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A([total numbers starts]) --> B[sum = 0]
  B --> C{{for each number in numbers}}
  C --> D{is there another number?}
  D -- yes --> E[sum = sum + number]
  E --> C
  D -- no --> F[/return sum/]
  F --> Z([back to the caller])
planChart.caption: the body of total: the yes branch adds one number and goes back to the loop setup, and only the no branch reaches the return.

steps.title: Turn the plain-English steps into pseudocode
steps.instructions:
Here is the plan in plain English:

**1.** Start the running total, `sum`, at 0.

**2.** Go through the numbers one at a time.

**3.** For each number, add it to `sum`.

**4.** When there are no more numbers, give back `sum`.

The same plan is drawn as a flow chart above the editor. You do not draw it, you read it: follow the arrows and match each box to one of the steps.

In `README.md`, type these as numbered pseudocode **between the first and last line**. Use SET for a change, FOR EACH and END FOR for the loop, and OUTPUT or RETURN for the answer. The chart shows the shape.
hints: The loop is `FOR EACH ... END FOR`, and the steps inside it are indented.
Whatever happens once the loop is over comes after END FOR, not inside it.

requirements.title: Five numbered steps in a row
requirements.description: Number every step 1. 2. 3. and so on, with something written after each number.
requirements.hint: You need at least five lines that start with a number, one after another, each with a step written after it.

requirements.title: Start sum at 0, before the loop
requirements.description: A step like `SET sum TO 0`, before the `FOR EACH`.
requirements.hint: Start with SET sum TO 0, and put it before the FOR EACH.

requirements.title: One loop over numbers, opened with FOR EACH and closed with END FOR
requirements.description: Exactly one `FOR EACH ... IN numbers`, closed with `END FOR`.
requirements.hint: Use one FOR EACH number IN numbers, and close it with END FOR.

requirements.title: Each number is added to sum inside the loop
requirements.description: A step like `SET sum TO sum + number`, between `FOR EACH` and `END FOR`.
requirements.hint: Between FOR EACH and END FOR, add the number to sum, for example SET sum TO sum + number.

requirements.title: RETURN sum happens after END FOR
requirements.description: Give back `sum` once the loop is over.
requirements.hint: RETURN sum goes after END FOR, once there are no more numbers.

requirements.title: Nothing is returned inside the loop
requirements.description: The only `RETURN` is the one after the loop.
requirements.hint: A RETURN inside the loop would end the method after the first number. Move it after END FOR.
